title: Is There One Best Way to Manage? | Principles of Management Ep 13
description:
Ravi's favourite team chat works beautifully on a slow afternoon, but fails in the morning rush at Chai Corner. In this animated lesson we use his chai stall to understand the contingency approach: there is no one best way to manage, because it all depends on the situation.

You will learn what contingent means, how the idea grew in the 1960s and 1970s from Burns and Stalker (1961), Joan Woodward (1965), Lawrence and Lorsch (1967) and Fred Fiedler (1967), the if-then thinking behind it, and the four things that shape a situation: size, technology, environment and people.

This is Episode 13 of our Principles of Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.

In this video:
0:00 One style, two times of day
0:19 No one best way
0:22 What is the contingency approach?
0:37 Burns and Stalker, Woodward, Lawrence and Lorsch, Fiedler
1:10 If-then thinking
1:18 Size, technology, environment and people
1:38 If-then at Chai Corner
1:57 Two outlets, two approaches
2:12 Quick check
2:24 Recap
